Playbook.name: Brute Force Attacks - Windows - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1110 Brute Force

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A source generated a burst of Windows authentication failures (4625 interactive/network, 4771 Kerberos pre-auth) against one or more accounts. The triage question is whether this is an attacker guessing passwords against a target account, an application looping with stale credentials, or an approved scanner - and, critically, whether any attempt succeeded (4624).
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A successful Windows brute force yields a valid domain or local credential and interactive/remote access to a banking host. Concentrated guessing against a privileged or service account, or credential stuffing against a single account from many sources, is a direct path to hands-on-keyboard compromise.

Assets.AssetType: Active Directory domain controllers (Kerberos pre-auth failures)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows logon auditing shipped to logs-system.security-* with 4625/4771/4624 present (verified live: 4625 volume ~11M/7d, source.ip populated on network failures).
winlog.event_data.TargetUserName and winlog.event_data.LogonType populated; source.ip populated for network-borne failures (verified live).

Signal.Name: Failure burst
Signal.Details: Many 4625/4771 failures from one source.ip or against one account in a short window.

Signal.Name: Success after failures
Signal.Details: A 4624 from the same source for an account that was being guessed - the escalation from attempt to compromise.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Source IP generating the authentication failures (source.ip from the alert).

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: Account being targeted (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName / user.name from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Failure volume and window from the alert; whether failures are 4625 (NTLM/interactive) or 4771 (Kerberos)
Whether the source is external, an internal app server, or an approved scanner

InitialAssessment.Rule: If failures concentrate on 1-3 service accounts with an identical error from an application server, lean Misconfiguration (stale-credential loop). Related pattern: the JCB spray playbook covers one-source-many-accounts.
If there is ANY 4624 success from $source_ip for a guessed account, or high-volume guessing against a privileged account, escalate immediately.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether $source_ip conducted a deliberate Windows password-guessing attack, whether it obtained a valid credential, and whether the target account is under distributed attack.

Step.name: Profile the failures from the source
Step.Purpose: Establish the brute-force shape: many failures against one/few accounts = classic guessing; identical errors on 1-3 service accounts = credential loop.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code IN ("4625","4771") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS fails=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), last_seen=MAX(@timestamp), hosts=VALUES(host.name), codes=VALUES(event.code) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT fails DESC | LIMIT 100
Step.AnalystNotes: High per-account counts on one or a few accounts = targeted guessing. A handful of service accounts with steady identical failures over hours = stale-credential loop (Misconfiguration). Many distinct human accounts = spraying (route to the spray playbook).

Step.name: Check for any successful logon from the source
Step.Purpose: A 4624 success from the guessing source is the difference between attempted and successful credential access.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code == "4624" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logons=COUNT(*), first_success=MIN(@timestamp), types=VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT logons DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Compare first_success against the failure window in INV-01. A success DURING or AFTER the burst for an account that was being guessed is strong TP evidence. Machine accounts (name$) authenticating are normal noise.

Step.name: Assess distributed pressure on the target account
Step.Purpose: Determine whether $target_user is being attacked from many sources (distributed brute force / credential stuffing) and whether it has any success.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4625","4771","4624") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events=COUNT(*), sources=COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip), src_list=VALUES(source.ip) BY event.code | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Many distinct sources failing against one account = distributed attack; a 4624 row appearing here means the account authenticated during the attack window - cross-check the source of that success against the failing sources.

Step.name: Measure host and account breadth from the source
Step.Purpose: Separate a source hammering one host (broken client behind it) from one walking many hosts (attack infrastructure).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code IN ("4625","4771") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS fails=COUNT(*), users=COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), logontypes=VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType) BY host.name | SORT fails DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One receiving host + few users = broken client or app loop on/behind that host. Many hosts receiving guesses, especially with LogonType 3 (network) or 10 (RemoteInteractive/RDP), = attack infrastructure.

Node.Condition: INV-02 (or INV-03) shows a 4624 success for a human/privileged account that INV-01 shows was being guessed from the same source during the window.
Node.Result: True Positive (credential compromised - escalate to IR immediately)

Node.Condition: INV-01/INV-04 show sustained high-volume guessing against one or few accounts (especially privileged) from an unowned or external source, with no success yet.
Node.Result: True Positive (brute force attempted, no success confirmed)

Node.Condition: Failures concentrate on 1-3 service/application accounts with identical Status/SubStatus for hours from an application/management server (stale stored credential).
Source is the documented Nessus scanner 192.168.166.1 or another approved assessment host, failures align to a scheduled scan, and no success follows.
Node.Result: False Positive (authorised assessment, proven no success)

Node.Condition: Source cannot be attributed from CMDB/ownership, or the shape is borderline (mixed service and human accounts), or a success needs owner confirmation.

FalsePositive.Definition: An approved scanner or assessment tool generated the failures by design and no attempt succeeded - authorised and proven non-impacting, not merely assumed benign.

Indicators.Item: Source is 192.168.166.1 (Nessus) or another documented assessment host.
Failures align exactly to a scheduled scan window.
INV-02/INV-03 show no 4624 success for any targeted account.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the scan schedule with vulnerability management.
Propose a scoped exception for the scanner source only.

TruePositive.Definition: A deliberate password-guessing attack against Windows authentication from one or many sources.

Indicators.Item: High-volume 4625/4771 failures concentrated on a target account, especially a privileged or service account.
Any 4624 success from the guessing source for a targeted account (upgrade to compromise).
Distributed pressure: many distinct sources failing against one account (INV-03), consistent with credential stuffing.

SOCAction.Item: Block or isolate $source_ip at the firewall/switch; if distributed, block the source set and rate-limit at the edge.
Force password reset and session/ticket revocation for any account with a success.
Open an incident; pull the source host for forensics if internal.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An internal system authenticating with wrong/stale credentials on a loop - operational, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: Same 1-3 service accounts failing continuously with identical Status/SubStatus from an app/management server.
No human accounts targeted and no successes.

SOCAction.Item: Open a ticket with the application owner to fix the stored credential.
Track under the credential-hygiene program; fix the source rather than exception the rule.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Block/quarantine $source_ip if external or unowned; block the source set if the attack is distributed.
Check INV-02 accounts for active sessions and revoke them.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reset passwords for accounts with post-attack successes and revoke Kerberos tickets.
Forensic triage of the source host if internal (identify the process driving the authentication).

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Review account lockout/smart-lockout policy and edge exposure of RDP/SMB.
Add confirmed stale-credential loops to the credential-hygiene remediation list.

Escalation.Trigger: Any 4624 success from a guessing source, high-volume guessing against a privileged account, or a distributed attack against a single account.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Scan/assessment schedule verified with the owning team and matches the source and window.
No 4624 success from the source in INV-02/INV-03.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Compromised accounts reset, sessions and tickets revoked.
Source contained (single or distributed set) and the driving process identified if internal.
